newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey seeks Iran's help against Kurdish rebels.
newsitem.headline: Turkey seeks Iran's help against Kurdish rebels.

text.p: Turkey sought Tehran's support on Sunday to prevent Kurdish rebels from escaping across the border into Iran from northern Iraq during an anti-guerrilla operation launched by the Turkish armed forces.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Omer Akbel said in a statement the Iranian charge d'affaires had been called to the ministry and told of Ankara's wish that Tehran prevent Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels seeking refuge in Iran.
"The charge d'affaires was also told we expected the Iranian security forces to take precautionary measures against elements able to provide support for the PKK from Iranian territory," Akbel said.
Ankara has in the past accused Iran of giving support to the PKK rebels, who launch raids into Turkey from both Iran and Iraq.

Turkey's Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan has sought to boost Ankara's relations with Tehran since he came to power last June, but the ties have been soured by the mutual expulsion of diplomats.
Iran has also protested against Turkey's steps to boost military ties with Israel.
The five-day-old military operation against rebel bases in northern Iraq has drawn criticism from Ankara's Western allies and the United Nations.

The military has said they have killed 902 guerrillas so far for the loss of 12 members of the security forces. It said on Sunday that one army helicopter had crashed in northern Iraq due to a "technical fault", killing two pilots.

The Germany-based DEM agency, which is close to the PKK, said in a statement on Saturday that more than 40 Turkish soldiers had been killed in clashes with the rebels. It gave no figures for PKK losses.
Tough restrictions on communications and travel have made it impossible to confirm the scale of the operation or the casualty figures.
